def count_colorings_optimized(n):
    num_subsets = 1 << n
    count = 0
    for coloring in itertools.product([0, 1], repeat=num_subsets):
        # f[T] = sum_{X subset T} coloring[X]
        f = [0] * num_subsets
        for T in range(num_subsets):
            # Sum over subsets of T
            s = T
            while True:
                f[T] += coloring[s]
                if s == 0: break
                s = (s - 1) & T
        
        # Check condition: f[T1] * f[T2] == f[T1 | T2] * f[T1 & T2]
        possible = True
        for T1 in range(num_subsets):
            for T2 in range(T1 + 1, num_subsets):
                if f[T1] * f[T2] != f[T1 | T2] * f[T1 & T2]:
                    possible = False
                    break
            if not possible:
                break
        if possible:
            count += 1
    return count

for n in range(1, 5):
    print(f"n={n}, count={count_colorings_optimized(n)}")
